text:
A5 done, commit e96143b. `./gradlew assembleDebug lint test` green: 0 lint
errors (23 pre-existing version-freshness warnings, same as prior tickets),
51 unit tests / 10 suites incl. new SyncEngineTest (push-only, pull-only,
dirty-preserved-when-local-newer race, 410 full-resync, 401 unauthorized)
and the two new "every mutation schedules a sync" tests in ItemsRepoTest/
ListsRepoTest.

Real bug (not test-only): androidx.hilt:hilt-work:1.4.0's Gradle module
metadata declares `requires 2.59` for com.google.dagger:hilt-android, which
wins Gradle's default highest-version resolution over our pinned 2.57.2 —
but the Hilt Gradle plugin + hilt-android-compiler stayed at 2.57.2, so
KSP-generated Hilt_MainActivity.java called a 2.57.2-only runtime method
(getSavedStateHandleHolder()) against the 2.59 jar and failed javac.
Tried bumping hilt=2.59 everywhere instead: that broke the Hilt Gradle
plugin itself against AGP 8.13.2 (ClassNotFoundException on
com.android.build.api.artifact.ScopedArtifact$POST_COMPILATION_CLASSES —
AGP 8.13.2's public ScopedArtifact only has CLASSES/JAVA_RES, so plugin
2.59 references an artifact-scope member that doesn't exist on this AGP).
Fixed by keeping hilt=2.57.2 and adding `configurations.all {
resolutionStrategy.force(...) }` in app/build.gradle.kts pinning
hilt-android/dagger/hilt-core/dagger-lint-aar to 2.57.2 project-wide, so
compiler/plugin/runtime all agree. Lesson for future androidx.hilt.*
extension additions (hilt-navigation, future hilt-* artifacts): check
`./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration debugRuntimeClasspath | grep
dagger` after adding any of them — these extensions routinely declare a
newer minimum hilt-android than whatever core hilt/hilt plugin version
the project is pinned to, and the mismatch only surfaces as an opaque
generated-code compile error, not a dependency-resolution warning.

Manually verified against the live dev server (:8723, self-signed TLS):
logged in as shopping@p23q.org, POSTed an empty-changes /api/v1/sync
request with the real bearer token, got back a real cursor + populated
changes.items/changes.lists payload. Its JSON shape (field name set,
category_order naming, stores as a JSON array under FieldClock) matches
ItemFieldsDto/ListFieldsDto exactly — no drift between the DTOs (written
in A3 against the spec) and the actual running server.

Design note carried forward: SyncEngine's merge is per-field, not
per-row — mergeItem/mergeList compare each field's (updatedAt, updatedBy)
tuple independently, so a single row can end up with a locally-newer name
and a remote-newer status after one sync. Row `dirty` becomes false only
if every field's merge picked the remote side; otherwise it stays dirty
and the winning local fields get pushed again next cycle.
